title: On the Ground in Beirut
partialText: Our Beirut bureau chief, Christina Goldbaum, reports on the escalating conflict between Israel and the Iran-backed armed group Hezbollah, as Israel’s military seizes areas of southern Lebanon and carries out bombings.

title: Trump Wants a Quick Victory in Iran. But the War May Be Costly.
partialText: The opening days of the conflict are challenging the idea that President Trump can project force abroad while safeguarding American lives and the economy.

title: Iran’s Friends Include China and Russia. But Where are They Now?
partialText: Iran maintains ties with a range of countries, including Turkey, India, Russia and China. Yet in this war, their support is mostly rhetoric.

title: Pro-American Kurdish Forces Are Preparing Possible Iran Incursion
partialText: The C.I.A. has given small weapons to Iranian Kurdish forces in Iraq in a covert program that began before the current war.

title: Hegseth Says War Will Go On ‘Until We Decide,’ and a Tariff Refund Update
partialText: Plus, why you should not let A.I. do your taxes.

title: What to Know About the Texas Runoffs in May: Key Races and Candidates
partialText: Texas voters will revisit the Republican Senate primary — and some House races where no candidate captured more than 50 percent of the vote — in runoffs on May 26.

title: Primaries Offer Warning Signs to Incumbents in Both Parties
partialText: Even as some top targets held on, lawmakers in both parties were pushed into runoffs by challengers in Texas, while some in the North Carolina state legislature lost.

title: Can Anthropic Make Peace With the Pentagon?
partialText: The artificial intelligence start-up has reportedly resumed talks with the Defense Department over use of its tools, with high stakes for both.

title: House Panel Votes to Subpoena Pam Bondi Over Epstein Files
partialText: The Oversight Committee took the action over the objections of its Republican chairman, after several G.O.P. members sided with Democrats to insist on it.

title: F.D.A. Faces Upset Over Denials of New Drugs
partialText: Agency officials promise fast reviews of new treatments while vowing they will not be a “rubber stamp” for the industry. But patients with rare diseases view recent decisions as signs that the doors are closing on their options.

title: Harry Styles Left as a Dominant Male Pop Star. He Returns to a Crowd.
partialText: In the four years since the British singer last released an album, artists like Sombr, working in similar aesthetic modes, have climbed onto the charts.

title: South African President on Trump’s Oval Office ‘Ambush’ and ‘Racist’ Policies
partialText: In an interview with The New York Times, President Cyril Ramaphosa opened up about the role of middle powers, relations with Washington and apartheid.

title: Why Ecuador Invited the U.S. Military to Help With Its Drug Gangs
partialText: Drug gangs have turned the South American country into one of the most dangerous in the region and the world’s leading exporter of cocaine.

title: James Luckey-Lange Recounts Being Detained, Starved and Beaten in Venezuela
partialText: James Luckey-Lange, 28, wrote about kindness and shared humanity as he traveled. But he said he had been shackled, starved and beaten in Venezuela after being detained.

title: ‘No Tax on Overtime’ Rule Isn’t What Some Workers Were Expecting
partialText: President Trump’s simple campaign promise, now reality, includes lots of fine print that is confounding taxpayers and companies this filing season.

title: A Word to the Wise: Don’t Trust A.I. to File Your Taxes
partialText: The world’s smartest technology is no match for the U.S. tax code.

title: Why Does Child Care Seem Less Affordable Than Ever?
partialText: It has always been expensive, but recently prices have risen faster than inflation.

title: L.A. Broker and Reality TV Star Accuses Oren Alexander of Sexual Assault
partialText: Tracy Tutor said Mr. Alexander, a former top real estate agent in New York, drugged and assaulted her in 2014. Mr. Alexander and his two brothers are on trial for sex trafficking.

title: Suspect Is in Custody After 3 Women Are Found Dead in Utah
partialText: A suspect was detained in Colorado a day after two women were found dead on a hiking trail, and a third at a residence in Wayne County, the authorities said.

title: A Dog-Sledding Adventure in Northern Minnesota
partialText: On the edge of the Boundary Waters Canoe Area, a novice learns to drive her own team on an adventure in the heart of winter.

title: Does the Iran War Put America First?
partialText: How the antiwar right sees Trump’s foreign policy.

title: Mass Hysteria. Thousands of Jobs Lost. Just How Bad Is It Going to Get?
partialText: Michael Steinberger on how A.I.’s impact on white-collar jobs may transform politics and society.

title: Late Night Doesn’t Understand Why America Is Attacking Iran
partialText: “This could be the first war ever launched based on vibes,” Jimmy Fallon said.

title: They Helped Her Open a Weed Shop. Now They’re Suing for $2.5 Million.
partialText: A dispute between the nonprofit Housing Works and the owner of a cannabis dispensary shows the risks for businesses in an industry that is locked out of traditional financing and resources.

title: Lawsuit Accuses Amy Griffin, Best-Selling Author, of Invasion of Privacy
partialText: A former classmate contends that Ms. Griffin’s story of being sexually abused, described in “The Tell,” was based on assaults the classmate herself suffered.

title: China Bets on Technology to Resist U.S. Pressure
partialText: China announced a 7 percent increase in military spending and a five-year plan to try to reduce its military and industry’s reliance on Western technology.

title: Trader Joe’s Expands Recall of Frozen Asian Foods Over Glass Risk
partialText: No injuries had been confirmed, but consumers reported finding glass in their products. The announcement was part of a larger recall of nearly 37 million pounds of food products.
